subject: Immediate: GPU pool failover causing reserved throughput gap — Finova impact & exec bridge
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finova.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: SRE Lead <sre-lead@finova.com>, procurement@finova.com
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Production impact: generation latency and errors since 08:45 PST

Karthik —

We started seeing elevated latencies and a spike in 502/504 errors on our production inference routes around 08:45 PST this morning. This is impacting transaction scoring and user flows (visible in our dashboard). TPS dropped by ~40% and average response p95 rose from 220ms to 1.8s.

Can you confirm whether this is related to our reserved capacity? Our contract (FN-2389) shows the dedicated pool should be pinned but we're seeing fallbacks to on-demand. We need an ETA for mitigation and whether this will persist for the morning.

We are available to join a bridge immediately.

— Alex
Alex Johnson
VP Product, Finova
alex.johnson@finova.com
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: naomi.feldman@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, soojin.lee@redwood.com
Cc: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finova.com>, SRE Lead <sre-lead@finova.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 09:24:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production impact: generation latency and errors since 08:45 PST

Folks —

Thanks Alex for the heads up. Naomi, can you triage immediately (root cause + whether reserved pool pins are being honored)? Initial ask: confirm whether autoscaler or host preemption led to a fallback, and whether the control plane mistakenly routing reserved requests to on-demand.

Marissa — please prepare an external-facing summary for Finova and let's get an exec bridge at 10:00 PST (15:00 UTC) if the impact persists.

I'll keep Alex and Finova SRE on this thread; will share findings in next 15–30m.

Karthik
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
From: naomi.feldman@redwood.com <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, soojin.lee@redwood.com
Cc: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finova.com>, SRE Lead <sre-lead@finova.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 09:39:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production impact: generation latency and errors since 08:45 PST

Karthik — brief findings so far: 

- Timeline: at 08:42 PST a subset of nodes in Finova's dedicated GPU pool received a cloud-level preemption during a planned host maintenance window. The autoscaler responded but misread the pool's "pinned" metric (regression in the enforcement check).
- Effect: ~22% of pinned capacity was not immediately re-provisioned; traffic was routed to on-demand variants and a small percentage of requests hit older model variants that lack the optimized KV cache layout.
- Symptoms: increased tail latency (p95 ~1.8s), transient 502/504 errors from overloaded on-demand nodes, and small increase in token retry loops (client-visible retries increased error amplification).

Actions in flight (ETA 30–45m):
1) Force the control plane to honor pinned reservations for FN-2389 (hotfix rolling now).
2) Warm a replacement set from the stable pool (starting immediate; should reduce fallbacks in ~12–18m).
3) Rollback the autoscaler enforcement change to the prior stable check (5–10m deploy window).

I've attached a short debug snapshot (debug_snapshot_20270214.tar.gz) with allocator traces and the routing map.

I'll post a second update at 10:00 PST or sooner if anything changes.

— Naomi
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finova.com>, SRE Lead <sre-lead@finova.com>
Cc: naomi.feldman@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, soojin.lee@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Status update and bridge invite — immediate mitigations and ask

Alex — quick update and next steps: 

- Root cause: cloud host preemption triggered an autoscaler regression that temporarily allowed routing off-reservation. Naomi's team has a hotfix in rollout to force the reservation check and is warming replacement nodes. We expect most traffic to return to reserved pool within 20m.
- Interim mitigation: we are throttling lower-priority traffic in the same availability zone to give Finova reserved lanes breathing room. This is a manual override and will remain until the warm-up completes.
- Customer impact: Finova's p95 should improve gradually; we will keep 1:1 monitoring with your SRE.

Request: can Finova leadership join an exec bridge at 10:15 PST for a 30–45m coordination call (we want to confirm readiness and discuss a short-term credit and priority headroom while we stabilize)? Bridge: https://zoom.redwood.com/bridge/FINOVA-2389-20270214

Marissa — I will need authorization for a one-time service credit and temporary reserved headroom (2x for 2 hours) to prevent recurrence while we complete the warm-up.

Karthik
From: marissa.cole@redwood.com <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: leadership@redwood.com, finance@redwood.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, naomi.feldman@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 12:01:00 -08:00
Subject: Approval request — Finova emergency credit and temporary capacity bump (FN-2389)

Team —

Finova (FN-2389) is experiencing production impact due to the reserved pool fallbacks described below (see Naomi's debug note). Customer is requesting an exec bridge and has asked about a short-term mitigation that includes: 
- 2 hours of 2x reserved headroom (priority slot allocation)
- 20% service credit to account for visible business impact during the outage window

Rationale: Finova is a mid-enterprise account with multi-product integration; preventing an expansion churn risk is a priority. Previous precedent: we approved similar short-term headroom and credits for Priority customers in Q3 last year.

Attachments: service_credit_proposal.pdf (draft credit language)

Ask: can Finance & Legal sign off in the next 30m so we can confirm on the 10:15 PST bridge? If not, I'll propose an interim goodwill credit and we will formalize the amount post-incident.

— Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finova.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: SRE Lead <sre-lead@finova.com>, procurement@finova.com
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 16:48:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Immediate: GPU pool failover causing reserved throughput gap — Finova impact & exec bridge

Thanks Karthik, Naomi and Marissa — appreciate the rapid response and the temporary headroom. We saw p95 drop back to ~260ms after 10:30 PST and error rates are back to baseline. Our payment flows look stable.

We'll join the bridge at 10:15 and Finova leadership will be there to review next steps. We also want a short RCA with timeline and a follow-up on the credit language.

— Alex
